runtime: CPython 3.x built-ins and C modules (typeshed symbols)
conventions: Symbols are the typeshed-qualified names Pyright resolves to (module of the .pyi + qualified name). Everything with Python source in the interpreter's Lib/ or site-packages is derived, never listed here.

entries.why: C builtin: builtins has no Python source

entries.describe: next(iterator) advances the iterator (__next__ / generator body)
entries.why: C builtin: builtins has no Python source

entries.describe: filter(function, iterable) calls the function on every item when consumed
entries.why: C builtin type: builtins has no Python source

entries.describe: sorted(iterable, key=...) consumes the iterable and calls key on every item
entries.why: C builtin: builtins has no Python source

entries.describe: min/max(iterable, key=...) consume the iterable and call key on every item
entries.why: C builtins: builtins has no Python source

entries.why: C method of the list type: no Python source

entries.why: C builtins: builtins has no Python source

entries.why: C builtin type: builtins has no Python source

entries.why: C methods of builtin types: no Python source

entries.why: C method of the set type: no Python source

entries.why: C builtin descriptor: builtins has no Python source

entries.why: C builtin descriptors: builtins has no Python source

entries.why: C builtin type: builtins has no Python source

entries.describe: chain/compress/zip_longest/product iterate every argument
entries.why: itertools is a C module: no Python source

entries.why: itertools is a C module: no Python source

entries.why: itertools is a C module: no Python source

entries.why: itertools is a C module: no Python source

entries.why: implemented in the C module _collections: collections re-exports it without Python source

entries.why: C methods of _collections.deque: no Python source

entries.describe: defaultdict(factory) calls the factory for every missing key
entries.why: implemented in the C module _collections: no Python source

entries.why: implemented in the C module _contextvars: contextvars only re-exports it

entries.describe: starts a new OS thread that calls the function (threading.Thread composes with this leaf)
entries.why: _thread is a C module: no Python source

entries.describe: installs the handler; the interpreter calls it when the signal arrives (signal.signal composes with this leaf)
entries.why: _signal is a C module: no Python source

entries.describe: atexit.register(function, ...) calls the function at interpreter exit
entries.why: atexit is a C module: no Python source

entries.describe: ref(obj, callback) calls the callback when obj is collected (obj itself is never called)
entries.why: implemented in the C module _weakref: weakref only re-exports it

entries.describe: pool.apply(function, ...) runs the function in a worker process
entries.why: the function is pickled into a task queue and called by the worker loop of another process; source cannot follow it through the pipe

entries.describe: pool.map(function, iterable) runs the function on every item in worker processes
entries.why: the function is pickled into a task queue and called by the worker loop of another process; source cannot follow it through the pipe

entries.describe: executor.submit(function, ...) runs the function in a worker process
entries.why: the work item is pickled into a call queue and run by _process_worker in another process; source cannot follow it through the queue

entries.describe: executor.map(function, *iterables) runs the function on every item in worker processes
entries.why: the work items are pickled into a call queue and run in another process; source cannot follow them through the queue

entries.describe: inspects the function object, never calls it
entries.why: the parameter is typed as a callable but only read (overrides the function-type rule)

entries.describe: reads or removes the function, never calls it
entries.why: the parameter is typed as a callable but never called (overrides the function-type rule)

entries.describe: wraps(wrapped) copies metadata of wrapped onto the decorated wrapper, never calls wrapped
entries.why: the parameter is typed as a callable but only read (overrides the function-type rule)

entries.describe: update_wrapper(wrapper, wrapped) copies metadata of wrapped, never calls it
entries.why: the parameter is typed as a callable but only read (overrides the function-type rule)

entries.describe: WeakMethod(method) keeps a weak reference to the method, never calls it
entries.why: the parameter is typed as a callable but only referenced (overrides the function-type rule)

io_send.describe: socket.connect(address): the outbound address of a raw socket (socket.create_connection and http.client derive down to it)
socket.connect_ex(address): the outbound address of a raw socket
socket.sendto(data, [flags,] address): datagram to the address
fork_exec(args, ...) starts a program on POSIX (subprocess.Popen derives down to it); args[0] names the program
CreateProcess(application, command_line, ...) starts a program on Windows (subprocess.Popen derives down to it)
os.system(command) runs a shell command line (implemented in the C module posix/nt)
os.execv(path, args) replaces the process with a program (C module posix/nt; the other exec* derive down to execv/execve)
os.execve(path, args, env) replaces the process with a program (C module posix/nt)
os.posix_spawn(path, argv, env) starts a program (C module posix)
os.posix_spawnp(file, argv, env) starts a program found on PATH (C module posix)

protocol command token (RESP, the Redis serialization protocol): a client sends PUBLISH channel message as the token followed by its arguments; the broker, a server outside the client package, delivers the message to the subscribers of channel. Key: the argument right after the token

protocol command token (RESP): SPUBLISH shardchannel message publishes to the subscribers of a shard channel (broker-side semantics, no source in the client package). Key: the argument right after the token

io_entry.describe: WSGI (PEP 3333): a server calls the application object (a callable, pattern __call__/2 without self) with (environ, start_response); the route key is environ['PATH_INFO'], the verb environ['REQUEST_METHOD']
ASGI specification: a server awaits the application (pattern __call__/3 without self) with (scope, receive, send); the route key is scope['path'], the verb scope['method']
socket.accept(): inbound connections of a server loop
socket.recv(): a consumer receive loop reads messages here

route_patterns.describe: angle-bracket placeholder with a converter (int, path, uuid ...)
brace placeholder with a converter or pattern

ffi_conventions.describe: ctypes loads a shared library by path (CDLL derives down to it)
ctypes looks up an exported C function by name: element 0 of the (name, library) tuple; CDLL.__getattr__/__getitem__ derive down to it
importing module m from m.<abi>.so / m.<abi>.pyd calls its C function PyInit_m (CPython C-API, PEP 489)

test_conventions.describe: pytest default discovery when no pytest configuration sets python_files/python_functions: functions test* and classes Test* in test_*.py
pytest default discovery: functions test* and classes Test* in *_test.py
unittest discovery default: methods named test* of TestCase subclasses in test*.py, with setUp/tearDown around each (looked up by name)

runtime_dispatch.describe: pytest passes the value of the fixture whose name equals a test parameter; fixtures in conftest.py are visible to its directory subtree; `name=` renames the fixture

syntax_conventions.describe: grpc_tools.protoc generates the client class <Service>Stub in *_pb2_grpc.py; calls on its instances are the service's rpcs
grpc_tools.protoc generates the server base class <Service>Servicer; its subclasses implement the rpcs
Strawberry builds the schema from classes decorated @strawberry.type (a root type class named Query / Mutation / Subscription)
a method decorated @strawberry.field resolves the field of the same name
a method decorated @strawberry.mutation resolves the mutation field of the same name
a method decorated @strawberry.subscription resolves the subscription field of the same name
Strawberry exposes snake_case resolver names as camelCase fields by default
Graphene calls the method resolve_<field> of an ObjectType subclass for the field <field> (looked up by name at run time)
Graphene exposes snake_case field names as camelCase by default
an ariadne QueryType() object holds the resolvers of the Query root type
an ariadne MutationType() object holds the resolvers of the Mutation root type
an ariadne SubscriptionType() object holds the resolvers of the Subscription root type
an ariadne ObjectType("Name") object holds the resolvers of the type named by its first argument
@obj.field("name") registers the decorated function as the resolver of that field of the object's type
